Kronikol command-line tool.

Usage: kronikol merge <inputs...> [-o <output.html>] [-t <title>]

  Combines several mergeable TestRunReport.json files (produced with
  ReportConfigurationOptions.GenerateMergeableData = true) into one combined HTML report.

Arguments:
  <inputs...>          Files, directories (searched recursively), or glob patterns.
Options:
  -o, --output <path>  Output HTML path (default: TestRunReport.html).
  -t, --title <text>   Report title (default: "Test Run Report").
  -h, --help           Show this help.

Example:
  kronikol merge ./artifacts -o TestRunReport.html -t "Nightly"

Usage: kronikol ingest <inputs...> [--tests <file>] [-o <dir>] [--render <mode>] [-t <title>] [options]

  Replays NDJSON interaction captures (one JSON object per line, the httpInteraction shape
  plus testId/testName) into a full Kronikol report: TestRunReport.html, the data files and
  the component diagram. Any capturer in any language can produce the input.

Arguments:
  <inputs...>              Files, directories (searched recursively for *.ndjson / *.jsonl), or globs.
Options:
  --tests <file>           Tests NDJSON (start/step/end records) supplying outcome, duration and steps.
  -o, --output <dir>       Output directory (default: ./Reports).
  --render <mode>          browserjs (default, needs internet at view time) | nodejs | local | server.
  -t, --title <text>       Report title.
  --feature <name>         Feature name for tests without one (default: Ingested).
  --collapse | --no-collapse   Collapse consecutive identical calls into a loop fragment (default: on).
  --collapse-threshold <n> Minimum run length to collapse (default: 2).
  --max-arrows <n>         Cap request/response pairs per diagram; the rest is summarised.
  --browser-render-workers <n>  Web Workers the browserjs report renders diagrams on (default: 4, capped by
                           the viewer's CPU count); 0 renders on the main thread as before 3.0.45.
  --note-format <json|yaml>  Initial display format for JSON note payloads in

result.stdout:
Usage: kronikol export <inputs...> --otlp <endpoint> [options]

  Pushes NDJSON interaction captures to an OTLP/HTTP collector as OpenTelemetry spans, so the
  traffic only Kronikol saw (proxy/TCP-tap hops, handler-captured calls) appears in Tempo/Jaeger
  next to the app's real traces. One request/response pair becomes one CLIENT span; captured W3C
  trace ids are preserved, and pairs without one group into one trace per test.

Arguments:
  <inputs...>              Files, directories (searched recursively for *.ndjson / *.jsonl), or globs.
Options:
  --otlp <endpoint>        The OTLP/HTTP traces endpoint, e.g. http://localhost:4318/v1/traces.
  --header <name=value>    Header added to every export request (repeatable) — auth tokens etc.
  --include-bodies         Export request/response bodies as kronikol.request.body /
                           kronikol.response.body span attributes (default: off).
  --body-cap <n>           Cap per body attribute when --include-bodies is on (default: 8192).
  --include-span-sourced   Also export records captured from the backend's own telemetry (an OTLP
                           tap); default off — re-exporting them duplicates spans the backend has.
  --per-pair-traces        Keep each pair's own trace id instead of grouping one test into one trace.
  --no-redact              Do not redact credential headers before mapping (default: redact).
  --redact-header <name>   Additional header to redact (repeatable).
  --gzip                   Gzip the POSTed payload (Content-Encoding: gzip).
  --dry-run                Write the encoded OTLP/JSON instead of POSTing (to --out, else stdout).
  --out <file>             Where --dry-run writes the document.
  -h, --help               Show this help.

Example:
  kronikol export ./captures --otlp http://localhost:4318/v1/traces --header "authorization=Bearer t"
